Dariali Gorge and the Gveleti Waterfalls

The narrowest gorge in the Caucasus, right at the border, with two waterfalls and a short, dramatic trail.

Time needed
2 h
From Tbilisi
170 km · 3:25
Road
Mostly paved
Car needed
Crossover / SUV
Season
May–October
Entry
პარკირება ~5 ₾

Dariali is where the mountains almost close the road. North of Stepantsminda the Terek valley suddenly narrows and squeezes between granite walls three hundred metres high. This is historically the main gateway through the Caucasus, called the Caspian or Caucasian Gates by ancient authors. The gorge runs up to the Russian border, and this is the last point on the route that a rental car can legally reach.

Halfway along, above Gveleti village, are two waterfalls:

  • The lower Gveleti falls, about fifteen minutes from the road and manageable for almost anyone
  • The upper Gveleti falls, roughly 25 metres high, another twenty to thirty minutes further up over boulders

The trail is short but not flat: loose blocks, tree roots and wet rock in the shaded sections. May and June are the best months, when snowmelt gives the falls their maximum volume; by late August the upper cascade thins noticeably.

Also in the gorge stands the Dariali Monastery, a modern complex built in the 2000s. It is new, but it sits surprisingly well against the cliffs and makes a natural last stop before the frontier zone begins.

Practical advice

Wear proper closed shoes with grip — sandals are useless on this trail. Near the falls the air is cold and the spray soaks clothing, so bring a windproof layer. This is a border zone: carry your passport or ID, as the border police do check. There is a small paid car park at the trailhead, usually with a kiosk. Buy food and water in Stepantsminda, because there is nothing at all further up the valley.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Stepantsminda follow the main road north along the Terek — 12 to 15 km, about twenty minutes. From Tbilisi it is 170 km in total and roughly three and a half hours. The main road is asphalt, though rockfall debris on the surface is routine here. The Gveleti turning is on the left after the bridge, and the last couple of kilometres are gravel, which is precisely why a crossover is preferable to a sedan. Do not drive up to the border crossing itself: taking a rental car out of Georgia is not permitted.
